open.speaker: sf_professor
lines: THAT'S THE WAY TO DO IT! ...Sorry, love. Reflex. Anyone stands in front of the booth, Punch comes up. Professor Swazzle, the real name's worse.
Forty-three years on this sand. Punch, Judy, the crocodile, the baby, the policeman, and every summer a new lot of kiddies who think the crocodile's real.
The crocodile is real. Don't tell them.
He's got the voice in his cheek even when he's not using it. You can see the shape of the tin.

passives.line: A pointed hat, a stick, a voice that is not a man's, and children taken off at the end. He is telling you the old shape of the thing in the Levels and he thinks he is telling you a joke.
There is a tin on a cord round his neck, worn to a shine. The swazzle lives there. He has had two stolen and he will not have a third.

options.text: Is the baby real as well?
Forty-three years. You'll have seen everything on this beach.
(Wait for Punch to go back down.)

wry.speaker: sf_professor
lines: The baby's a sock. Everything else is real. That's the trade.
You've a face for the booth, you have. Deadpan. I'd put you on as the policeman.

kind.speaker: sf_professor
lines: Everything and twice. I've seen a man propose with a crab. I've seen the pier catch fire and the band play on because they hadn't been told.
And I've seen 1973, which is what you're after. Sit on the sand, the deckchairs are Wilf's and he counts.

silent.speaker: sf_professor
lines: ...He's gone. He goes if you don't feed him.
You're patient. Patient's rare. Patient I'll talk to.

hub.speaker: sf_professor
hub.prompt: Go on, my love. Next show's at the half hour and Judy's lost a hand.
lines: Go on, my love. Next show's at the half hour and Judy's lost a hand.

static.line: He lost two swazzles in 1973 and he knows who took them and he knows what came back. Make him put the tin in his mouth. Make him do the voice.

options.text: Who taught you the voice? Punch men don't learn it from a book.

fail.line: Trade secret, my love. A Punch man tells you where he learned the voice and the next week there's two booths on the sand.

options.text: Do it for us. Not Punch. The flat one. The voice with no breath in it.
Two swazzles gone in '73, and you've kept the third round your neck ever since. You know who took them.
Listen to this. The station telephone box, last night.
We'll let Judy find her hand.

taught.speaker: sf_professor
lines: Old Codman, Llandudno, 1949. Put the tin under my tongue and said swallow it and you're dead, breathe through your nose and you're Punch.
I swallowed one in '51. Didn't die. That's the whole of the training. The voice isn't yours, it's the tin's, and you're just the breath going through.
That's why the camp lads wanted one. Put a tin in, and whatever comes out, it wasn't you said it.
A voice you can disown. That's exactly what a man in a hat on a marsh would want.

voice.speaker: sf_professor
lines: ...That's what they said it said, isn't it. Colin's story. I've done that line once a year, to the sand, to see if it still frightens me. It does. Gulls went up, did you see.
It wasn't the gulls. Something on the Levels turned its head.

voice_fail.speaker: sf_professor
lines: No. Not that one. I'll do you Punch, Judy, the crocodile. I'll do you the Queen. Not that one.
Wilf's brother did that one for thirty years on the pier and look where Dennis is. Ask Wilf. He won't tell you either.

lost.speaker: sf_professor
lines: ...The lad in the hat. Sunny Jim, they called him. Borrowed one in May, said it was for the kiddies' club, and I let him, because he had the knack and the knack's rare.
He brought it back the Wednesday night. Wet. Put it on the sand in front of the booth like it was hot and said, Professor, it talked without me. I stopped and it kept on.
I never put that one in my mouth again. It's in the tin with the other. Two in the tin and I've never worked out which is which.
One of those tins has a voice in it that doesn't need a man. He wears it round his neck.

lost_fail.speaker: sf_professor
lines: Lost. I said lost. Lost is lost, my love, and I've had forty years of kiddies' fingers in my booth, things go.
If you want who was borrowing what that summer, ask Len Cutmore at the camp. He packs the costumes. He packs everything.

tape.speaker: sf_professor
lines: ...Play it again. ...No. Switch it off. Off.
That's not a swazzle. A swazzle's got a man behind it, you can hear him breathing through his nose if you know. There's no nose on that. There's no man on that.
That's the tin on its own. That's what he brought me back. Put it away. Please.
Forty-three years in the trade and he's asking us to put a cassette away. I'm putting it away.
